question: What is the primary role of a nurse in dietary counselling?

options.A: Diagnosing rare metabolic disorders through dietary history
options.B: Purchasing food items for hospitalized patients from local markets
options.C: Prescribing complex micro-nutrient formulas for hospital patients
options.D: Translating medical dietary orders into practical lifestyle habits

explanation: Nurses bridge clinical orders and daily life by helping patients apply dietary advice practically. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h1)

question: Why must nursing dietary counselling consider local food availability and culture?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of hospital catering services
options.B: Hospital policies mandate the use of traditional ingredients
options.C: Foreign foods are strictly prohibited in clinical guidelines
options.D: Patients are more likely to follow advice that fits their lifestyle

explanation: Plans that align with a patient's cultural and financial reality improve adherence outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h1)

question: Mid-upper arm circumference is an example of which assessment type?
explanation: Body measurements like weight, height, and arm circumference fall under anthropometry. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h2)

question: A patient looks well-nourished outwardly, so what should the nurse do next?

options.B: Perform a complete nutritional assessment including history and labs
options.C: Discharge the patient without giving any dietary advice
options.D: Assume the patient has no nutritional deficiencies

explanation: Outward appearance does not rule out hidden micronutrient deficiencies, requiring thorough investigation. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h2)

question: Which type of question is best for uncovering a patient's eating habits?
explanation: Open-ended questions encourage patients to share detailed information about their actual daily routines. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h3)

question: A patient seems hesitant to change their diet due to cultural attachments. What is the best nursing approach?

options.A: Ignore their cultural preferences and hand them a printed brochure
options.B: Explore their ambivalence using motivational interviewing techniques
options.C: Tell them strictly that their cultural foods are unhealthy
options.D: Discontinue dietary counselling until they change their mindset

explanation: Exploring ambivalence respectfully helps patients find acceptable compromises without feeling alienated. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of collaborative goal setting in dietary care?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any further nutritional assessments
options.B: It helps the patient take ownership of their health journey
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never experience illness again
options.D: It removes all responsibility from the nursing staff

explanation: When patients help create their goals, they are far more motivated to achieve them. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h4)

question: Why are small, achievable targets preferred over a complete diet overhaul?

options.A: Patients prefer spending less time talking with nurses
options.B: Doctors do not support major dietary modifications
options.C: Small changes are easier to maintain over a long period
options.D: Complete overhauls are illegal in clinical practice guidelines

explanation: Gradual adjustments prevent patient fatigue and support long-term behavioral adherence. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h4)

question: A patient cannot afford prescribed protein sources due to financial constraints. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the patient to the hospital social welfare unit immediately
options.B: Discontinue all dietary counselling until their finances improve
options.C: Suggest affordable local protein alternatives available in the community
options.D: Tell the patient to borrow money to buy the expensive food

explanation: Problem-solving requires finding practical, affordable local substitutes that fit the patient's budget. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h5)

question: Why is it important to involve family members in dietary counselling sessions?

options.A: Family members are financially responsible for hospital bills
options.B: Patients lack the cognitive ability to remember instructions
options.C: Hospital regulations require family presence during education
options.D: Family members often buy and prepare the household meals

explanation: Since others in the home usually prepare the food, family involvement ensures sustainable dietary changes. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h5)

question: What is the purpose of follow-up visits after dietary counselling?

options.A: To review food diaries, check weight trends, and reassess labs
options.B: To discharge the patient from all medical follow-ups
options.C: To punish the patient for failing to follow the meal plan
options.D: To collect additional consultation fees for the clinic

explanation: Follow-ups allow nurses to measure progress and catch any emerging issues early. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)

question: How should a nurse react when a patient fails to meet their dietary goals?

options.A: Treat it as useful feedback to adjust the care plan
options.B: Stop providing any further nutritional support
options.C: Scold the patient for wasting the nursing staff's time
options.D: Assume the patient is intentionally lying about food intake

explanation: Unmet goals highlight flaws in the current plan, signaling a need to adapt strategies to reality. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T005#GNS227_U7_T005_h6)
